title: A HARD knot its ceilings cannot stop fell back to a one-tick render that ran away; a knot accepted during an explicit brake dropped the brake (Nucleus val-hlj)

title: truncateAfter dropped the knot at its own time: every segment bundle starting where the queue ends replaced the author's knot with a C2 hand-off, and a C1 script lost its corners at every knot
description: Bench 2026-10-06, Phosphor 0.1.195 declaring c1_cubic, Nucleus 0.1.20: the sine funscript still hitched after every peak and trimmed/stretched (47 trims, 46 stretches in 884 plans). title: Kinetic² solver scratch is thread_local (10 KB of TLS): every FreeRTOS task must host it in its stack, the IPC task has 1 KB, the P4 asserts in esp_ipc_init and boot-loops
description: Found on the bench 2026-10-06 flashing Nucleus 0.1.16 (the first Kinetic²-only image): assert in esp_ipc_init (xTaskCreatePinnedToCore of ipc0) before app_main, rebooting every ~1.4 s. jerk::solve keeps its banded matrix as static thread_local (solver.hpp ~220, A[kMaxUnknowns][2*kHalfBand+1] + b), so the image carries a 10,240 B .tbss; ESP-IDF places each task's TLS block inside the task's own stack, so a task whose stack is smaller than the TLS cannot be created. Fix: a jerk::Workspace owned by the Engine (one per axis, in .bss) and passed down through solveWindow and jerk::solve; no static, no thread_local, no stack.
close_reason: Fixed in Kinetic 3c85cff: jerk::Workspace per axis; .tbss gone from the P4 image (0.1.17).

title: Frame move keeps the curve in flight through the reaction horizon (RFC-105 (bb)): reseedAt re-planned from now, so a window write inside a knot's horizon trimmed it to rest on the reseed (Nucleus val-4dt reversal -336 mm/s, val-83q held tick)
description: Engine::reseedAt re-solves the pending window from now, skipping the reaction-horizon commit every other re-plan takes (commitHorizon). title: A bundle start a few microseconds off the newest knot drops a committed reversal (submit reads the committed corner as a brake) or hands the next piece an over-amax junction that winds up (a^2/2J)
description:
Operator play 2026-10-08 on Nucleus 0.1.28 (Kinetic 06673ee, factory 1200 / 1e5 / 2e7 on a 100 mm window): the plan overshoots authored reversals by up to 0.35 of the window ("perfect 99 percent of the time, overshoots sometimes"), held at the window edge by the arbiter backstop. Hub replays of the ADSR script (fs_adsr_1/2.json) show the plan strip passing a reversal knot (0.95, v = 0) at +3.19 w/s and turning at 1.29.

Two kernel defects, both reached when a segment bundle's start stamp misses the newest knot by microseconds (clock jitter between bundles; every sender has it):

(M1) Start a few us BEFORE the newest knot: Nucleus calls truncateAfter(start). Its commitHorizon commits through that knot (the fixed rule: later half of its piece), the window empties, and it returns 0. The submit that follows sees an empty timeline and a piece with a tail (the reversal's corner ramp into rest) and runs replanFromBrake, which undoes the commit and re-plans from now + react straight to the next target. The reversal knot is gone and the curve passes it moving. Same misread as kin-g1f (a HARD knot committed through on its authored time), which the live jog redirect depends on.

(M2) Start a few us AFTER the newest knot: Nucleus inserts a hold knot there (its own rule, fixed in Nucleus). After a moving knot that is a 1 ms piece (kMinSpanUs floor) to rest at the same position: PieceOverCeiling, and its end acceleration (several times amax) becomes the junction state. The next piece's lead ramp unwinds it at jmax and gains a^2/2J of speed (3892 w/s2 gained 38 w/s and ran the plan to 2.96 windows). The same state would feed a starvation brake (Profile::brake) and Profile::point.

Fix: a committed curve is never a brake (submit); a HARD knot is reached at its solved time in commitHorizon (kin-g1f, so the jog redirect truncates instead of leaning on the misread); a junction state is held to the ceilings (emitRun); a profile never starts from an acceleration past amax (brake, point).
close_reason: Fixed in b041a20 (submit never re-plans a committed curve; commitHorizon reaches a HARD knot at its solved time; junction states held to vmax/amax in emitRun; brake/point start from a held to amax). Nucleus b097a81 pins it and adds the one-tick start rule. Host-verified: Kinetic 4/4, Nucleus native green, arbiter rig ADSR 168 mm -> 135 mm. Bench replay owed at the flash.

description: What kin-88m listed that its model port (c38a450) did not do. (2) NOT removable, kept with a constraint comment: the zero stroke is illegal while the previous angle heads in faster than the span turns it (vcap lands a round later); final-round fallbacks: 108 in 5000 scripts (99 legal picks), 110 in the property suite (48 legal); without it PieceOverCeiling 48 -> 472, violations 34 -> 396 (seed 6 first). title: Engine piece builder reshapes the render: a lone 200 ms segment from rest renders as a 150 ms crawl then a 736 mm/s spike (the operator's quick-then-crawl)
description: Piece::bezier (engine_piece.hpp) falls back, when the end accelerations cannot be matched, to moving the start length toward the start acceleration (i0 to kLMax or kLMin) before the lead ramp. The renderer sized the start ramp's room for ITS lengths (handles::startRoom), so the piece the engine renders is a different curve than the one the render chose: for the incident rig's lone segment (134 to 176 mm in 200 ms, window 84 mm, from rest) the solver's piece is the symmetric smoothstep (peak 315 mm/s, 6300 mm/s2) and the engine rendered i0 = 0.95 with a 78 us lead: 52 mm/s at 50 ms, 736 mm/s at 160 ms, 31000 mm/s2 decel. Legal under the ceilings (the solver's second pass judges what the engine builds), so no test caught it; Nucleus test_motion_arbiter's incident cases (v > 100 mm/s at 50 ms) did. Fix: keep the render's lengths; the lead ramp carries the step, else the start correction. Fingerprint re-accepted with it.

title: Kinetic2 renderer: silent junction steps and coarse ceiling tightening
description: Property suite (tests/test_kinetic2.cpp:551): 78 of 800 random runs go over a ceiling or the window with no PlanFailed; 2 do not end at rest (:553). Seen cause (seed 6): a corner ramp exits at the rendered curve's acceleration and the next piece (28 ms) can neither match it by its start length nor fit a lead ramp, so an acceleration step is left (finite-difference jerk 58k vs 6k). Also: the slack tightening over-trims (acceleration-bound span trims 0.35 to 0.17 where about 0.30 is reachable under jmax, tests/test_kinetic2.cpp acceleration-bound case). A final judge-everything pass was tried and reverted: it reports PlanFailed on legal sampled curves (the solver's built pieces differ from what the engine renders after re-plans). Discovered in kin-mol-ri8 step D.
notes:
2026-10-07 (verifier round): silent junction steps fixed. Every built piece is judged as the 1 ms grid reads it (piece, lead, start correction, steps with the jerk beside them, the last knot's brake) and anything still over after the slack passes is reported PieceOverCeiling; an unmatched start the lead cannot carry is carried by a quintic start correction (handles::Piece::da); authored angles are held to the rail stop; an illegal hold lies flat; overOf finds the position's turning points exactly. Property suite: 0 silent of 800 runs, 0 not at rest, 382 reported (rule 5, ruling owed). Still open here: slack tightening over-trims at flat knots (the acceleration-bound span keeps 0.17 of 0.35, about 0.30 is reachable).
2026-10-08 (verifier round 2): slack tightening is per ceiling now (HKnot::slack[3]); speed and acceleration tighten from what the render itself reads of the piece (at most half per pass), so a lead ramp that puts the built piece over makes the render bind; a built piece within half the tolerance of a ceiling tightens too (the u grid reads under the 1 ms grid). The acceleration-bound span renders its top at 0.180 (was 0.170) with jmax binding at 1.0001; 0.30 is the jerk-optimal profile's reach, not a Bezier's, so the test floor pins 0.175. Corner ramps: the room each needs (start ramp at the piece before's end acceleration, ramp to rest into a flat knot, the origin's lead from rest) is part of a piece's legality (handles::Room); a start ramp with no room asks the piece before for a nearer end acceleration next round (HKnot::aTarget). title: solve_budget: a resumable, bit-identical bound on one planner run (RFC-108 item 8)
description:
Valence RFC-108 item 8: Config::solve_budget bounds ONE planner run (the solve runs on the planner task since RFC-105 (ggg), not the 1 ms tick); unit: judged pieces. A run that spends its budget stops; the next run continues the SAME computation (same knots, same round) and the window publishes only when it ends, so the render is bit-identical to an unbounded one. Cutting the window instead is forbidden (the newest knot rests, the G2 sweeps couple every knot).

Not small, so not in the kin-tnv change (operator's condition: implement only if small and provably bit-identical). Design:
1. State. Everything the render reads already lives in Workspace (HKnot k[], t_us[], built[]) or is recomputed from the window. Add a cursor to Workspace: {gen (the window generation it renders), run start i, run end j, the origin s/s_us of the current run, pass (0..kSlackPasses), stage (solve | nudge piece r | emit | tighten), round, extra, r (the next piece of nudge)}. solveWindow's outer loop (chase / HARD / renderRun) and renderRun's pass loop and handles::render's round loop become re-entrant on that cursor; handles::nudge gains a start piece and a piece budget (one fitPiece call = one judged piece; a memo hit costs 0).
2. Progress. Every run judges at least one piece, so a budget below one piece still finishes.
3. Engine. A solve that returns incomplete leaves solved_valid false and keeps sampling the committed curve (the previous published window's pieces up to the reaction horizon); the next solve resumes when gen is unchanged, else restarts from the new window. A window finishing past react_us is a late plan under RFC-105 (ggg).
4. Proof. A parity test: every fixture and bench scenario rendered at budget 1, 2, 7 and 96 against budget 0, Solved compared field by field with memcmp, plus the fingerprint at every budget. Bit-identity holds because the split executes the same float operations in the same order with all state in caller memory (no static, no thread_local, -ffp-contract=off).
5. Risk to measure first: a segment stream whose knots arrive faster than a computation finishes restarts it every time (gen moves) and never publishes. Measure on the P4 (bench_kinetic2 scenarios A and D, plan_us) before choosing between restart and finishing the stale computation first.
Consumers: Nucleus planner task (val-8rt) passes the budget; the twin stays unbounded.

title: Handles playground: a funscript as a composite cubic Bezier in the time-position plane, knot classes G0/G1/G2 per knot, draggable handles, the ceilings as bounds on the handle lengths, a tolerance box for the nudges
description: A second static page beside the Kinetic2 playground (playground/handles.html, handles.js, handles-model.js) for the handle model under study (the 2026-10-07 design conversation): the script's knots stay on the author's clock, each knot has one angle (velocity) and two handle lengths (time influence, fractions of the adjacent spans; a third is the exact PCHIP cubic), G0 marks a corner with two angles, G1 one angle with free lengths, G2 acceleration continuity (angle for a through point, lengths for a crest), auto classifies from the chords (hold edge, crest, through). The ceilings bound the lengths per piece (speed from above, acceleration and jerk from below); a piece that no length satisfies may move its knot within a tolerance box; what remains is shown as infeasible. The page loads a .funscript, lets the operator set each knot's class and drag its handles (aligned, Blender style), and shows velocity, acceleration and jerk against the ceilings with every nudge visible. Pure JS model, no wasm: this is the design playground, not the kernel. handles.check.mjs runs the model on the built-in script and asserts the figure numbers (a 150 mm / 200 ms stroke between crests fits at a length of 0.25 under 1000 mm/s and 50000 mm/s2) and, with Playwright available, that the page loads with zero console errors.
notes:
Operator rulings 2026-10-07. (1) Through points are G2 by default, crests and hold edges stay G1 (PCHIP as drawn, the corner ramp takes the step); a Makima/Akima-style request makes every knot G2: the style select (pchip | smooth), hold edges flat in both, the window is a ceiling, the inspector shows handle lengths in ms. (2) Amplitude: when no handle length is legal, the later knot moves toward the previous knot's actual position by the least that is legal (bisection; time kept, height lost); a reachable knot never moves; the feel floor (lfloor, default 0.15) bounds how short a nudged handle may get before amplitude gives. Replaces the fixed box. Check: a run of 100 mm strokes at 150 ms against 400 mm/s trims every top to 47 mm with the bottoms anchored at 0. Open: a through point trims toward the previous knot too, which lengthens the next piece; balancing it between its two pieces is the alternative if a script shows the need. Centering a trimmed stroke instead of anchoring it at the previous knot is the operator's call.
Window mock 2026-10-07: rail, window size and offset sliders rescale the script live; a rail strip shows the window band and the carriage; Play runs the render at real speed (Space). Found: angles must be held to the speed ceiling (a G0 chord or a G2 angle over vmax has no legal piece); a trimmed knot's hold moves with it so the hold stays flat; angles are re-solved from the trimmed chords (two rounds); a trim that reaches nothing legal still takes the least-over position. Three windows on the built-in script (100, 300, 500 mm) render inside the ceilings with 0, 9 and 13 trimmed knots.

title: Kinetic² stream at the velocity ceiling from far away collapses: a 1000 mm/s sample stream starting 110 mm from a resting carriage drops samples and sags to rest (bare kernel, vmax 2, amax 100, jmax 10000, 57 ms latency)

title: Kinetic² never catches up on a dense stream once one knot is infeasible: a 60 Hz 1 Hz sine from rest crawls for 2 s at jmax 500
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). Knots p = 0.5 - 0.35 cos(2 pi t) at 60 Hz from rest at 0.15, defaults (vmax 3, amax 30, jmax 500, Blend floor 0.25). The cosine starts with a = 13.8 u/s^2, so the first knot cannot be met from rest under jmax (about 28 ms of ramp). Expected: a few tens of ms of lag, then tracking. Observed p every 250 ms: 0.150 0.158 0.176 0.201 0.222 0.263 0.296 0.325 0.378 (target 0.15 0.5 0.85 0.5 0.15 ...), the same authored ahead, streamed with KINETIC2_KNOT_SAMPLE (16 ms latency: ... 0.404), under Stretch, and on the previous kernel (not a regression). The same sine at 10 Hz tracks exactly (0.150 0.502 0.850 0.500 0.150 ...), and at jmax 5000 the 60 Hz one tracks. Reading: each later knot is judged from the lagging state and spent again (stretch shifts every later knot, Blend trims toward the previous end), so the lag compounds instead of closing. 60 Hz is the funscript scrub rate. Playground preset Scrub shows it.
notes:
2026-10-06: the crawl was the kernel's stream model, not the sine: with the stream replay (persisted samples, eased compression, min-jerk interior junctions, free tail velocity with a resting acceleration) the 60 Hz sine at jmax 500 should track after its infeasible first knots; re-measure with the real module and close if it does.
2026-10-06 re-measured with the stream model (bare kernel, 60 Hz 1 Hz sine of 0.35 from rest, streamed at 16 ms latency): jmax 500 still crawls (98 of 120 samples refused, peak speed 1.08 of 2.2); jmax 1000 and 5000 track with zero refusals. A piece's jerk at 60 Hz is about 300,000 times the mismatch between its mean speed and its end speeds, so a one-percent speed inconsistency saturates 5000 and a sixth of a percent saturates 500: the ceiling binds, not the model. The playground default is jmax 2000 and the README states the bound. Left open for the operator: document as the floor for 60 Hz streams, or lower the stream rate under 1000.
2026-10-06 later: re-placing a trailing sample's prior time by the replay rule (solver.hpp sampleTime) made the 60 Hz sine track at jmax 500 as well (0 refused, peak speed 2.396); the sticky stretched priors were the crawl. The ceiling ruling stands.
close_reason: Operator ruling 2026-10-06: not a defect. Ceilings are normalized (windows/s^3): 500 is 200,000 mm/s^3 on a 400 mm window, far below any real configuration; Nucleus's input default is 2,000,000 mm/s^3 (5000 normalized) and the machine tolerates 5,000,000. A 60 Hz stream needs about 1000 normalized (400,000 mm/s^3 on 400 mm) because a 17 ms quintic's jerk is ~300,000 x its speed mismatch. The playground default stays at 2000.

title: Kinetic² Hard junction winds up backward (to the window edge) before the stroke; a script's last free knot lands moving and the brake overshoots it
description:

(1) Hard junction wind-up: reset(0.1, 0); one C1 knot v=0 at (600 ms, 0.5). The carriage first moves AWAY from the target: p min 0.0000 at 258 ms (the window edge), v min -0.671, then rises to 0.5. Suspect the polynomial head to (head_us, head) is fitted with a high head velocity in a short span, and the quintic from rest reaches it by winding up. The Staircase preset (five C1 v=0 steps of 0.15 every 300 ms from 0.1) dips to 0.0992 before its first step, the same effect small.
(2) Last free knot: reset(0.1); one free C2 knot at (600 ms, 0.5): the solver gives it v 0.667, the timeline then runs dry and SettleEngaged brakes past it to 0.5243 (overshoot 0.024). Same at the end of the Hard stop preset (0.9 lands moving at 0.667, brakes to 0.9243) and Overreach under Stretch (0.95 to 0.998). Whether the newest knot of an authored window should be solved to rest is a ruling: the engine comment calls the brake 'the only honest rendering' for a starved stream, but here nothing was starved, the script simply ended.

title: Kinetic² anomaly reporting: every re-solve re-reports each pending knot's spend; solver anomalies carry the knot's time, not the engine clock; ABI dropped flag is never observable
description: Found by the playground (kin-8ef). (1) solveWindow reports WaveformScaled/DeadlineStretched for every pending knot on every re-solve, so a streamed knot is reported once per submit while it is pending: 18 anomalies for 5 knots (starved stream), 830 for 60 (streamed scrub). types.hpp says 'one event per axis spent, so the counts read as a diagnosis'. (2) Anomaly::t_us is documented 'engine time at record', but solver kinds record the knot's solved time (e.g. 8304 ms = authored + the 8 s stretch cap, while the clock was at 200 ms); only SettleEngaged and KnotRefused carry the clock. (3) PlanFailed detail is the worst ceiling ratio (1e30 = kIllegal for no legal piece), not only the types.hpp sentinels. (4) ensureSolved erases dropped knots from the timeline and compacts sol[], so kinetic2_solved never returns dropped = 1; a reader can only learn of a drop from PlanFailed (target = authored p). The playground matches drops by that target.

notes: Looked at 2026-10-10 with kin-h1ii, not cheap: PieceOverCeiling's worst ratio is a max over ~10 judges in renderRun/emitRun (render overOf, built piece, lead, start step, corner ramp, last brake) plus handles' nudge fits for KnotTrimmed; naming the ceiling needs the argmax carried through each, and a field on Anomaly (fits in its padding, 24 B kept) that the wasm ABI (kinetic2_anomaly) and the RFC-108 event would carry. chaseRun's convergence and Engine::committedOver know their ceiling directly.

title: G2 (smooth) segment felt as a slight shift on the machine, observed before the kin-554/val-8ry overshoot fixes; revisit only if it returns
description: Operator 2026-10-08: a slight shift was felt when a G2 segment played, before the reversal-overshoot fix (kin-554/val-8ry, 0.1.29) and the render-fidelity fix (kin-b1d). Likely those, not the jerk step at a G2 seam: at jerk 2e7 a seam changes acceleration over milliseconds, well under the drive loop's bandwidth, and the loaded ladder rang nothing at the ceilings. If it returns on 0.1.29 or later: capture the same script with overshoot_capture.py (0x1100/0x4100 at 60 Hz), find the seam in the plan trace, and compare the planner's velocity across it with the hub position; a real seam artifact shows as a step in the plan's acceleration series, a stamp artifact shows as a hold or reversal. G3 is not the answer unless that measurement says so (the plant is a low-pass; G3 adds overshoot and quintic solves).
notes: kin-rfw7 (3ee99dd) does not explain this: before ca56157 the solver rendered every knot with the pchip style (kStyle = Pchip at 7f7330d), so 0.1.28-era firmware never ran the smooth path; a G2 (Smooth junction) knot there was pchip's through point. The smooth-path excursions kin-rfw7 fixed (speed and acceleration over, up to 4x amax on a reported piece) only exist at Config::smoothness above 0.
